title: Three Mondays and One Short Card
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：identity　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 identity 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the registrar ① proved the identity that no citizen in the office would have recorded, and he said the proving was the whole of the Monday. The ② identity, meaning the name itself and not the card, ran three Mondays and stayed unrecorded in the book; a identity, he said, is the only thing in a office that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ identity in that office had the same short card beside it, and the ④ identity at the far door, meaning the number they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A identity, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the registrar said the recording is the part that fills three Mondays.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the identity was the whole of the matter, meaning the belonging and not the name. The ⑥ identity, meaning the belonging and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; identity, he said, is either something you prove or the only word that means both a name and a belonging. He said the belonging is the part they remember.

By 1991 the ⑦ identity had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short card. The ⑧ identity of the whole thing, the registrar wrote in March, was one office and three Mondays of recording; identity, he said, is either the number at the far door or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ identity I remember is the name recorded in the list, which closed in 1993 and is still recorded as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ identity, my mother said in 1995, is the only name that improves by being recorded; every identity, she said, is a belonging that has agreed to look like a name. She said the belonging was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 身份；本体（指办事处里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 身份；本体（指那个姓名本身，与卡片相对）
C. 固定搭配：prove the identity 证明身份
D. n. 身份；本体（指留给孩子们收着的那一串那一个）
E. n. 身份之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的身份之事）
F. n. 身份；本体（指清单里写到、被记下的的那一个）
G. n. 归属、认同（指一件事里人人都认却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 认同（抽象总称，指人人都认却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: proved the identity that no citizen in the office would have recorded

answers.why: prove the identity 意为“证明身份”，1986 年那位登记员把办事处里没有一位市民肯记录的一个身份做了一遍。
identity 意为“身份；本体”，指那个姓名本身而不是卡片，它经过了三个星期一而在簿子上没有被记录。
identity 意为“身份；本体”，指办事处里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一张薄薄的卡片。
identity 意为“身份；本体”，指最远那个门口留给孩子们收着的那一串那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
identity 意为“归属、认同”，指一件事里人人都认却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份归属就是那件事的全部。
identity 意为“认同”，指人人都认却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个姓名，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
identity 意为“身份；本体”，指清单里写到、被记下的的那一个，到 1991 年这一个成了清单里的一行。
identity 意为“身份之事”，登记员三月写道，整件事的身份之事是一处办事处和三个星期一的记录。
identity 意为“身份；本体”，我记得的是清单里记录过的那一个，1993 年核实了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一个。
identity 为抽象总称，母亲 1995 年说，身份是唯一会因为被好好记录而变得更好的姓名。
